cards.text: Jesus just taught in the synagogue in Capernaum that He is the bread of life, and whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood has eternal life (John 6:48, 54, 59). Now MANY of His own disciples are talking it over. Picture every oven in my bakery beeping at the same time, friend.

cards.question: Many of His disciples hear it and say this is a ___ teaching, and they ask who can accept it.
The disciples are grumbling about this teaching. True or false: somebody has to go tell Jesus about it.

cards.text: Nobody has to tell Him. Me? I sat in a junk drawer for years and found out about EVERYTHING last.
Jesus asks them, "Does this offend you?" Then He asks what will happen if they see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before.

cards.question: Jesus says the flesh profits nothing. He says the ___ is what gives life.

cards.text: Jesus says the words He has spoken to them are spirit and they are life. Then He says some of them do not believe, and I bet that room got so quiet you could hear an oven timer tick.

cards.question: John stops the story to tell us something about Jesus. True or false: Jesus had known from the beginning which of His disciples did not believe.
Jesus reminds His disciples of something He told them before. No one can come to Him unless what?

answers.text: The Father has granted it to him
He keeps every law of Moses
He was born a son of Abraham

cards.question: From that time on, what do many of Jesus' disciples do?

answers.text: Turn back and stop walking with Him
Stay and ask Him to explain it
Go back to the synagogue to argue

cards.question: With so many disciples gone, Jesus turns to the ___ and asks, "Do you want to leave too?"

cards.text: Simon Peter, one of the Twelve, speaks up: "Lord, to whom would we go?" He answers a question with a question, and somehow it's the best answer in the room.

cards.question: Why does Peter say there's nowhere else for the Twelve to go?

answers.text: Jesus has the words of eternal life
Jesus fed thousands with five loaves
Jesus healed so many of the sick

cards.question: Peter goes on and tells Jesus what the Twelve believe and know about Him. What is it?

answers.text: He is the Holy One of God
He is a prophet like Moses
He is a teacher from Capernaum

cards.text: Jesus answers them and reminds them He chose them, the Twelve. Friend, if He said that to me, I'd be standing a little taller on my gold base.

cards.question: Jesus reminds the Twelve that He chose them. True or false: He also says one of them is a devil.
John tells us exactly which one of the Twelve Jesus was speaking about. Who is it?
Judas was one of the Twelve, but later he was going to ___ Jesus.

findings.problem: The question includes 'and they ask who can accept it.' That rules out 'familiar' and 'beautiful' on its own, so the only answer left is 'difficult.' The card tests nothing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer to card 3 ('Nobody has to tell Him') and adds a joke. It tells no new part of John 6:61 and doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This card only retells the text. It has no reaction, comparison or other trace of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: John appears for the first time here ('John stops the story'), but the card doesn't say who he is, such as the one who wrote this account.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'leave' is close enough to 'betray' that a baker could argue for it. Betraying Jesus means turning away from Him, and Judas does go out and leave in John 13:30.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
